raw_statement_token: "Let $V=\\{1,\\ldots,f\\}$, let $E$ be the set of two-element subsets of $V$, and let $\\mathcal{G}_f$ be the quotient of the real polynomial algebra in variables $x_{\\{i,j\\}}$ by the relations $x_{\\{i,j\\}}^2=x_{\\{i,j\\}}$. For each graph isomorphism class $[G]$, let $p_{[G]}$ be the corresponding invariant orbit sum, and let $\\mathcal{I}_f$ be the set of polynomials $p_{[G]}$ for graphs $G$ with at least one isolated vertex. **Algebraic form of the Kelly–Ulam conjecture.** If $f$ is at least three, then the subalgebra of $\\mathcal{G}_f$ generated by the polynomials of $\\mathcal{I}_f$ is $\\mathcal{G}_f$ itself. The source states that this is equivalent to the vertex-reconstruction conjecture, because these polynomials encode the numbers of subgraphs appearing in the vertex-deleted subgraphs."
decoded_statement: Let $V=\{1,\ldots,f\}$, let $E$ be the set of two-element subsets of $V$, and let $\mathcal{G}_f$ be the quotient of the real polynomial algebra in variables $x_{\{i,j\}}$ by the relations $x_{\{i,j\}}^2=x_{\{i,j\}}$. For each graph isomorphism class $[G]$, let $p_{[G]}$ be the corresponding invariant orbit sum, and let $\mathcal{I}_f$ be the set of polynomials $p_{[G]}$ for graphs $G$ with at least one isolated vertex. **Algebraic form of the Kelly–Ulam conjecture.** If $f$ is at least three, then the subalgebra of $\mathcal{G}_f$ generated by the polynomials of $\mathcal{I}_f$ is $\mathcal{G}_f$ itself. The source states that this is equivalent to the vertex-reconstruction conjecture, because these polynomials encode the numbers of subgraphs appearing in the vertex-deleted subgraphs.
